arabicText: هتيحل رعش نم ذخيأو هبراش زجيو هرافظأ ملقي لجرلا :هل لقا هنأ (ملاسلا هيلع) رفعج يبأ نع ،ةرارز نع .اريهطت هديزيل كلذ نإو - لقا نأ ىلإ - ةنس اذه لك ةرارز يا :لاقف ؟هءوضو كلذ ضقني له ،هسأرو
englishText: From Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) that he asked him: If a man clips his nails, trims his mustache, and takes from the hair of his beard and head, does this invalidate his ablution? He said: O Zurarah, all of this is Sunnah- then he said- and indeed that increases his purification.

chapter: Purity Of Iron
arabicText: قلحأو يبراش نمو يرافظأ نم ذخآ (ملاسلا هيلع) الله دبع يبلأ تلق :لقا جرعلأا الله دبع نب ديعس نع لىع حسمفأ :تلق ،ءوضو كيلع سيل ،لا :لقا ؟أضوتفأ :تلق ،لسغ كيلع سيل ،لا :لقا ؟لستغفأأ ،يسأر .حسم كيلع سيل روهط وه :لاقف ؟ءاملا يرافظأ .ةبوطرلا عم لاإ نوكي لاو ديدحلبا لاإ نوكي لا نلآا ىلإو تقولا كلذ يف قلحلا نأ مولعملا نم :لوقأ
englishText: From Sa'id bin Abdullah Al-A'raj, he said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): "If I cut my nails, trim my mustache and shave my head, should I perform ghusl (ritual bath)?" He said: "No, ghusl is not required of you." I asked: "Should I perform wudu (ablution)?" He said: "No, wudu is not required of you." I asked: "Should I wipe water over my nails?" He said: "It is purification, wiping is not required of you." I (Hurr Amili) say: It is known that shaving at that time and until now is only done with metal/iron and only with moisture.

chapter: Purity Of Iron
arabicText: .امد هيف رت مل ام هيف ليصت ءادرلا ةلزنمب فيسلا :لقا (ملاسلا هيلع) ايلع نأ دمحم نب رفعج نع
englishText: From Ja'far bin Muhammad, that Ali (peace be upon him) said: The sword is like a cloak, you can pray in it as long as you do not see blood on it.

chapter: Purity Of Iron
arabicText: ناك اذه :لاقف ،ماظع نم ةلحكمو ديدح نم لايم (ملاسلا هيلع) نسحلا وبأ ينارأ :لقا مهجلا نب نسحلا نع .تلحتكفا ،هب لحتكفا (ملاسلا هيلع) نسحلا يبلأ يف يذلا لحكلاو ،بادهلأاو نافجلأا رهاظلو عمدلاو نيعلا لخاد ةبوطرل هتقالام نم دب لا ليملا :لوقأ يف اهضعب مدقت ،ادج ةريثك ىنعملا اذه يف ثيداحلأاو ،كلذ نم ئش ريهطتب رمؤي ملو ،كلذ ريغو ةلحكملا ريصقتلاو قلحلا يفو ،فيسلا يف ةلاصلا زاوج يفو ،ةلاصلا يف ديدحلا باحصتسا يف اهضعب يتيأو ،ضقاونلا .اهنومضمب لمعلا لىع ةيماملإا عامجإ انئاملع نم ةعامج لقن دقو ،كلذ ريغو جحلا يف
englishText: From Al-Hasan bin Al-Jahm who said: Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) showed me From Al-Hasan bin Al-Jahm who said: Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) showed me an iron needle and a kohl container made of bones, and said: This belonged to Abu Al Hasan (peace be upon him), so apply kohl with it. So I applied it. I (Hurr Amili) say: The needle must come in contact with moisture inside the eye, tears, outer eyelids and eyelashes, and the kohl in the container and other things, and there was no command to purify any of that. There are many hadiths with this meaning- some were mentioned previously in the invalidators, and some will come in discussions about carrying iron during prayer, permissibility of praying while wearing a sword, and in shaving/trimming during Hajj and other topics. A group of our scholars have reported the consensus of the Imamiyyah on implementing their content.

chapter: Purity Of Iron
arabicText: هنانسبأ هرعش نم ضرقي لجرلا يف (ملاسلا هيلع) الله دبع يبأ نع ،رامع ثيدح ضقاونلا يف مدقت دقو .ديدحلا يف كلذ امنإ ،سبأ لا :لقا ؟ليصي نأ لبق ءاملبا هحسميأ هرثأ رهطي مل اسجن ناك ول هنلأ ،ديدحلا ةراهط لىع هتللاد ىفخي لاو ،بابحتسلاا لىع خيشلا هلمح :لوقأ .رم امل حسملبا
englishText: The hadith of Ammar has preceded in the invalidators, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) regarding a man who bites off some of his hair with his teeth, should he wipe it with water before he prays? He said: There is no harm, that is only with iron. I (Hurr Amili) say: The Shaykh interpreted it as recommendation. Its indication of the purity of iron is not hidden, because if it was impure, its trace would not be purified by wiping, as previously mentioned.

chapter: Purity Of Iron
arabicText: هافق قلح وأ ،هرعش نم زج وأ ،ديدحلبا هرافظأ صق لجر يف (ملاسلا هيلع) هنع رامع نع رخآ ثيدح يفو ،ةلاصلا ديعي :لقا ؟ءاملبا كلذ نم حسمي ملو لىص نفإ :لئس ،ليصي نأ لبق ءاملبا هحسمي نأ هيلع نفإ .ةنجلا لهأ سابل بهذلاو ،رانلا لهأ سابل ديدحلا نلا :لقاو ،سجن ديدحلا نلا ةساجنلا :لوقأ .ةريثكلا رابخلال فلاخم ذاش هنلأ :لقا ،باجيلاا نود بابحتسلاا لىع لومحم اذه :خيشلا لقا ليلعتلو ،لسغلبا رملاا مدعو حسملبا ءافتكلالو رم امل ةفاظنلا ينعأ ةيوغللا ةراهطلا مدع ىنعمب انه .كلذ ريغو رانلا لهأ سابل نم هنوكب ةساجنلا
englishText: In another hadith from Ammar from him (peace be upon him) regarding a man who cut his nails with iron, or trimmed some of his hair, or shaved the back of his head, it is upon him to wipe it with water before he prays. He was asked: If he prayed and did not wipe any of that with water? He said: He should repeat the prayer, because iron is impure. And he said: Because iron is the clothing of the people of the Fire, and gold is In another hadith from Ammar from him (peace be upon him) regarding a man who cut his nails with iron, or trimmed some of his hair, or shaved the back of his head, it is upon him to wipe it with water before he prays. He was asked: If he prayed and did not wipe any of that with water? He said: He should repeat the prayer, because iron is impure. And he said: Because iron is the clothing of the people of the Fire, and gold is the clothing of the people of Paradise. The Shaykh said: This is interpreted as recommendation, not obligation. He said: Because it is anomalous, contradicting many reports. I (Hurr Amili) say: Impurity here means the absence of linguistic purity, meaning cleanliness, as previously mentioned, due to sufficing with wiping, not commanding washing, justifying the impurity by it being from the clothing of the people of the Fire, and other than that.

chapter: Purity Of Iron
arabicText: يف ةلاصلا زوجت لا :لقا (ملاسلا هيلع) الله دبع يبأ نع ،ليكأ نب ىسوم ثيدح يف ليصملا سابل يف يتيأو .خوسمم سجن هنفإ ،ديدحلا نم ئش
englishText: In the chapter on the clothing of the one praying, in the hadith of Musa bin Akeel from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), he said: Prayer is not permissible in anything made of iron, for it is impure and transformed.
